whatsNew.title: What's new
whatsNew.help: What changed in Quizmoo, newest first.

1_12_0.title: Tours, help and tooltips
1_12_0.intro: Quizmoo now shows you around: a short tour on every main page, a help page that explains everything, and a tooltip on every button that shows only an icon.

sections.title: Tours
items: The first time you open a main page (home, quizzes, the editor, a new game, the lobby, the first question, results, My settings), a short tour points at its most important controls. Step through it or close it at any time.
The tours you have seen are remembered on your account, so a tour you saw on the laptop does not show again on your phone. My settings, Account has "Show all tours again".
Players get a short tour in the lobby while they wait, once per device.

sections.title: Help
items: The ? button at the top shows the page's tour again and opens Help.
The new Help page explains the app for players and hosts, with a small picture of the controls in each section, links to the pages in question and 22 frequently asked questions.
The Help page opens with a link back to your home.

sections.title: Tooltips
items: Tooltips are in Quizmoo's own look and follow the game's colours and the dark mode.
Every button that shows only an icon has one, and they open on mouse hover and keyboard focus, never on a tap.

fixed: The Quizmoo logo on the help, legal and projector pages takes a logged-in host to their home instead of the join page.

1_11_0.title: A starter quiz and clearer texts
1_11_0.intro: Every new host starts with a ready quiz that shows what Quizmoo can do, and every text in the app was reviewed so it reads the same everywhere.

sections.title: Starter quiz
items: New accounts get a 20-question starter quiz in their language: funny and tricky questions covering every question type, three rounds, pictures, double points and more.
The Starter quiz button on your quiz list adds a fresh copy any time, so you can try it again or start from it.

sections.title: Texts
items: Every text in the app was reviewed: plainer wording, the same word for the same thing on every screen.
Groups of questions are called rounds everywhere, in the editor too, and "Play again" starts a rematch.
The privacy notice and the terms of use say the same in both languages and are easier to read. Hosts accept the updated terms at their next login.

fixed: The role field in the admin's Add user dialog shows its label again.

1_10_1.title: Small fixes
1_10_1.intro: Fixes from testing, one front page for logging in, and every version on this page now says what was fixed.

sections.title: This page
items: Every version lists what was fixed after its news, the earlier versions included.

sections.title: Logging in
items: There is one front page for everyone: you log in on its Host tab. Old login links still work and open it.

fixed: A PIN that no game answers no longer stays on the join page after a refresh: the page starts empty. Join links from QR codes work as before.
The Quizmoo logo at the top of your pages takes you to your home page instead of the players' join page.
Switching between Play and Host on the front page is smooth: the card grows or shrinks to the other side instead of jumping.

1_10_0.title: A real finale on the projector and on every phone
1_10_0.intro: The end of the game is now a show: a podium with a drum roll, the leaderboard, awards and game facts on the projector, and four pages of results on every phone.

sections.title: On the projector
items: The podium builds up place by place, with a drum roll before the winner, the crown landing and confetti.

Then the leaderboard with everyone (or every team), the awards (Fastest finger, On a roll, Know-it-all, Climber) and the game in numbers: questions, players, share right, game length, the hardest and easiest question.

You decide what is on the projector: pick a page in the Podium card on the host page, or use the arrows, the page names and the Automatic button on the projector itself if you opened it from the host page. Space and the arrow keys work too.
Automatic shows a new page about every 10 seconds and starts again after the last one.

"Show the questions" goes through every question with its answers, one at a time, only when you want it. Each shows the right answer, how many got it right and a word about it, from "Easy peasy!" to "A real brain-teaser!".

There is one projector screen now: the separate results slideshow is gone. "Open projector" on the results page opens the game's projector while the game is still available (about an hour after it ends).

sections.title: On the phones
items: The last screen is four pages instead of one long list: Standings, Answers, Facts and My stats. Players move between them with the buttons, a swipe or the arrow keys.
Standings shows the player's place in a big card and the players just above and below them.
Answers lists every question, closed until tapped, with how many were right on top.
Facts shows the game's figures and awards, with "That's you!" on the player's own. My stats shows their best streak, answer times, their place after each question and the points per question.

fixed: The points inside the result stamp on the phones' answer list are readable in light mode.

1_9_0.title: Try your quiz in the editor, and a tidier question list
1_9_0.intro: Play your quiz on the editor's phone preview before the event, and work faster in the list of questions, even with 200 of them.

sections.title: Try your quiz
items: "Try it" above the phone preview plays the quiz from the selected question: answer on the preview, see whether it was right, the points and the correct answer, then go on with Next. Stop takes you back to the editor's preview.
It counts as a game would: speed and streak bonus, small typos in typed answers, and each group's own rules. Switched-off questions are skipped.
Change the question while you are on it and it starts again with your change. Nothing is saved and no game is started.

sections.title: The list of questions
items: Each card shows its number on the left, which turns into the grip when you point at the card. You can still drag the card from anywhere.
The question type's icon turns into the eye when you point at it: click it to switch the question off or on. Group headers work the same way for all their questions.
Cards are tighter, so the question text has more room.
The number of switched-off questions shows next to the list's title with "All on", so switching a question off no longer moves the list.
"Group" in the list adds the new group above the selected question instead of at the end of the list, with a name not used yet.

fixed: Dragging questions no longer stutters in long quizzes.
The page no longer scrolls along when you drag a question towards the bottom of the list, so the question lands where you drop it.

1_8_0.title: Seasonal themes
1_8_0.intro: On special days of the year Quizmoo takes on the season's look: its own colours, decorations and a dressed-up cow, on every page and in your games.

sections.title: Nine seasons
items: New Year, Carnival, Valentine's Day, Women's Day, April Fools' Day, Easter, Halloween, St Nicholas' Day and Christmas, each for about a week around its day.

Each season has its own colours in light and dark mode, decorations along the edges of the screen (cobwebs, lights and snow, bunting, flowers and more), falling leaves, snowflakes, hearts or confetti, and a short greeting on the join and login pages.

The cow dresses up for every season: Dracula at Halloween, a reindeer at Christmas, Mikulás on St Nicholas' Day, a jester on April Fools' Day, and more. It also has six new things to say in each season.
On the podium, part of the confetti takes the season's shapes: pumpkins and bats, hearts, Easter eggs, Christmas trees and stars.

sections.title: In your games
items: The new "Seasonal" theme is the default: during a season the host control, the projector and the phones show the season's look, and Classic at other times. Quizzes that used Classic now use Seasonal; quizzes on any other theme keep their theme.
With another theme you choose under Look which screens still show the season: the host control, the projector or the phones.

sections.title: Your choice
items: Don't want it? The season button next to the colour mode switches the seasonal look off on your device, and in the game menu on phones.
Admins find every season with its dates under My settings, Account: preview any season on their own device, change its dates, or switch it off for everyone.

1_7_1.title: Clearer release notes
1_7_1.intro: A small update to this page.
fixed: The notes of earlier versions are reworded so they describe the changes more clearly.

1_7_0.title: Typo tolerance and lock joining
1_7_0.intro: Typed answers with small typos now count, you can close a game to new players, and the editor shows the details of every picture.

sections.title: Typos accepted
items: Typed answers with small typos now count: "tokio" is right for "Tokyo". One mistake is allowed from 4 letters, two from 8, three from 12 and four from 18; numbers must be exact. A near miss scores the same as an exact answer.
"Accept small typos" is in the Scoring group and is on by default; switch it off and only exact answers count.
The player's phone says "Close enough" under Correct, and you see "Typo accepted" on the live board, next to the question's answers and on the results page.

sections.title: Lock joining
items: Close the game to new players with the "Lock joining" switch in the lobby, and open it again whenever you like. With late joining on, the running game's top bar has the same switch.
Players already in can always come back; new phones and the projector see that joining is closed.

sections.title: Pictures in the editor
items: Every picture is now a card: a bigger preview, its size in pixels, its file size and its format next to it (what the phones and the projector get), and Replace image and Remove image as buttons.
Hover an option's small picture to see the same details.

1_6_0.title: Next question, game length and screens between questions
1_6_0.intro: Choose which question comes next, see how long a game takes, and show the progress and the next question between questions.

sections.title: Choose the next question
items: Between questions, open the Questions tab and press "Play next" on any question still to come. The rest keep their order.

The tab shows what plays next at the top, finds questions as you type, and folds the played and upcoming lists. It also tells you before you pick when a question would leave its round or join the one under way.

sections.title: Game length
items: Your quizzes, the editor and the new game dialog show roughly how long a game takes, and the dialog updates it as you change the settings.
The lobbies say it too, and during the game the host, the projector and the phones see about how much is left.

sections.title: Between questions
items: The projector shows how far the quiz is, what kind of question comes next (never its text) and the top 3; phones show progress and what's next in small. Switch each part off under Look.
A 3-2-1 countdown before every question, on the projector and the phones: switch it on under Game flow. "Start now" skips it.

sections.title: Messages and the top bar
items: Quick message in the game's top bar sends one of your messages at once: hover it and pick how long it stays.
You see the message on your own page too, just like the players; its × clears it on every screen.
After each question the phones show which question it was above the result.
In the running game and the editor the app bar is part of the page's own top bar: the Quizmoo logo opens the language, the look and your pages.

fixed: The button that shows and hides the side panels in the running game works again.
Buttons no longer flicker when the pointer rests on their bottom edge.

1_5_0.title: The live board
1_5_0.intro: See at a glance who has answered and what while your game runs, without scrolling.

sections.title: Everyone on one screen
items: The running game fills your laptop screen: the question with its timer and answers per option at the top, the controls on the right, and every player in the middle.
Each player has a tile that fills in as their answer arrives: its colour, how fast, and right or wrong at once. Players still thinking have an hourglass, offline players are faded.
After the question the same tiles show who was right, the points and how the ranks moved. In team games the players are grouped by team, with the team's answer.
The tiles grow or shrink to fit: big for a family game, compact for a full room of 60.

sections.title: Views and options
items: View switches between tiles and a list, and sorts by name, rank, answer time or the missing answers first.
Hide answers shows only who has answered, for when players can see your screen.
Standings, messages, players, questions and the preview are tabs next to the board. Hide them for more room, and open the menu from the top bar when you need it.

1_4_0.title: Questions on and off
1_4_0.intro: Leave questions out of a game without deleting them, and find your way around big quizzes faster.

sections.title: Switch questions off
items: Every question has an In the game switch. Switch a question off and it stays in your quiz, but new games skip it: it is not shown, not counted and gives no points.
Switch a whole round off with its own switch, or with the eye on its card in the list. A round with every question off is skipped, intro included.
Switched-off questions are faded in the list. All on brings them all back for the next event, and Undo switches them off again.

sections.title: Editor improvements
items: Search the questions from the top of the list: by question, answer or round name, with or without accents.
New question and New group are in the top bar and at the top of the list, and the list's controls stay in view while you scroll.
The target button brings the selected question into view, and the selected card stands out more.
Set the time and points new questions start with, per quiz in its settings and for your new quizzes in My settings. The quiz title can be changed in the settings too.

1_3_0.title: Shuffled questions
1_3_0.intro: Play the questions in a new order every game, and see bigger pictures on the phones.

sections.title: Random question order
items: Turn on Shuffle question order in a quiz's settings, or only for one game when you start it. Every game then plays the questions in a new order.
A round moves as one block with its questions, and its questions are mixed too. Switch on Keep question order in a round when its questions must stay in order.
The Shuffle button above the question list mixes the quiz for good. It asks first, and Undo puts the old order back.

sections.title: Bigger pictures on phones and the projector
items: On phones the question number, the round, the timer and the settings button share one slim bar at the top, so the question's picture fills the width, with every answer still on screen.
On the projector the question, its picture and all the answers always fit on one screen.
When you pause, players see a big Paused sign in the middle of their screen, and nothing on it moves.

fixed: A game fills the whole phone screen: no empty strip stays at the bottom when the browser's address bar slides away.

1_2_0.title: Rounds
1_2_0.intro: Split a quiz into rounds, each with its own intro, rules and standings, and make quizzes of up to 200 questions.

sections.title: Rounds in your quizzes
items: Group questions into rounds, each with a title, info, a picture and a colour. Questions outside the rounds still work, for a warm-up or a bonus question.
Every round opens with an intro on the projector and the phones. It waits until you press Start round, or starts by itself after a few seconds; Hold stops the countdown.
The standings can follow every round by themselves, or come only when you show them. Answers can also be revealed at the end of a round instead of after each question.
Each round can have its own time, points and rules, such as no speed bonus in the bonus round. Your controls tell you when a round has rules of its own.
The lobby says how many rounds are coming, the question screens show the round, and the results group the questions by round.

sections.title: The editor
items: A round is one card in the question list: drag questions in and out, move a whole round, or fold rounds away.
Give questions a colour too, to find them at a glance. Only you see the colours.
Hide the phone preview with the eye button at the top, for more room for the list and the question.
Spreadsheets and Quizmoo files keep the rounds and the colours; the template shows an example round.

sections.title: Bigger quizzes
items: A quiz can now hold 200 questions in up to 50 rounds, and a long game stays as quick at the last question as at the first.

sections.title: Animated logo
items: The cow in the Quizmoo logo now changes its expression or shows a short line from time to time, and has a seasonal look on special days.

1_1_0.title: The first public beta
1_1_0.intro: Quizmoo is online for friends and family. Here is what you can do as a host.

sections.title: Make quizzes
items: Seven question types: single and multiple choice, true or false, free text, number, poll and put in order, each with a picture if you like.
The editor saves as you type, shows each question in a phone preview and lists what still needs fixing.
Import questions from a spreadsheet (Excel, Google Sheets) or a Quizmoo file, and download any quiz to share it.
Themes, answer colours and symbols, or your own colours, and your logo and event name on the projector.

sections.title: Run games
items: Players join with the PIN or the QR code on any phone, no app or account needed. Up to 60 players.
Pause, add 30 seconds, skip a question, send a message to every phone, and show a question again or the standings at any time.
Schedule a game up to 30 days ahead and share its link; players can add it to their calendar.
Lock your screen during a game, so nobody reads the answers off your laptop.
"Play again" starts a new round with the same players in one tap.

sections.title: Play in teams
items: You set the teams, the players make them, or both; anyone can also play on their own next to the teams.
Each team answers its own way: the captain decides, a majority vote, or everyone counts.

sections.title: See the results
items: A summary with the podium and the easiest and hardest question, then every player's, team's and question's details, and a CSV export.
Results are kept for 90 days, then deleted.

sections.title: Your account
items: My settings: quick messages, your usual game settings, branding, password and screen lock code.
Download all your data or delete your account at any time.
You can request a host account on the home page; an admin approves it.

sections.title: Good to know
items: Quizmoo installs on a phone or laptop like an app.
Found a bug or have an idea? Tell us through Feedback in the menu.

fixed: The selected answer on colourful buttons is marked inside the option instead of with a ring reaching into the next answer.
The quiz editor no longer shows two scrollbars when the settings are open next to a short question.
The app no longer loads as a blank page or with errors when many phones share one venue wifi.
Confirmation dialogs on phones have full-size buttons instead of squashed ones.
A host message leaving the screen is no longer cut off at the bottom.
The menu keeps the current page highlighted while you search the game history.
A gap that let the limit on login attempts be bypassed is closed.

privacy.title: Privacy notice
privacy.intro: This notice explains, as the GDPR requires, what Quizmoo stores about you, why, for how long, and what rights you have. In short: as little as possible, only to run the game, never sold and never used for advertising or tracking.

sections.heading: Who is responsible
paragraphs: The controller of your data is the operator named above, a private individual running Quizmoo as a free hobby project. Write to the contact above with any question or request about your data.

sections.heading: If you play
items: The nickname you type, the avatar you pick and your team. Everyone in the game sees them: the host, the other players and the shared screen. Use a nickname, not your full name.
Your answers, how fast you gave them and your points, to score the game and show the results.
A random player code in your browser, so you get back into the game after a reload.
Nothing else: no account, e-mail address, phone number, location or IP address is stored.
paragraphs: Legal basis: taking part in the game you chose to join (GDPR Article 6(1)(b)), and the host's legitimate interest in looking back at the results of their event (Article 6(1)(f)).

sections.heading: If you host
items: Your username, and your password only as a one-way hash that nobody can turn back into the password.
When you last logged in (shown only to the administrator, to see which accounts are still in use), and which version of the terms you accepted and when (as a record of our agreement).
Your logins: a random code per browser, stored as a hash, for up to {{sessionDays}} days.
Your quizzes, the pictures you upload, your settings, and the games you ran with their results.

Administrators only, if they enter one: an e-mail address for notices about new sign-ups. It is used for nothing else and is deleted when the administrator removes it or is no longer an administrator.
paragraphs: Legal basis: the agreement to use the service, i.e. the terms of use (Article 6(1)(b)); for the last login, the record of accepting the terms and the security measures, the legitimate interest in running the service securely (Article 6(1)(f)).

sections.heading: Pictures and quiz content
paragraphs: Hosts decide what goes into their quizzes. If a picture or a question shows or names someone, the host must be allowed to use it. To have something removed, ask the host or write to the contact above.

sections.heading: Security
items: The connection is encrypted (HTTPS), and passwords and login codes are stored only as hashes.
To stop password guessing and abuse, the server counts requests per network address for a minute, in memory only. Addresses are never written to the database or the logs.
The hosting provider may log network addresses for its own security, under its own privacy policy.
If a personal data breach puts your rights at risk, the operator reports it to the supervisory authority within 72 hours and notifies the data subjects concerned where the law requires it.

sections.heading: How long
items: Finished games, with the players' nicknames and answers, are deleted {{days}} days after the game at the latest, and only the newest 200 games are kept for each host.
Unfinished games are closed after 12 hours and then deleted in the same way as finished ones.
Pictures that no quiz, setting or game uses any more are deleted within two days.
Expired logins are deleted daily. A sign-up the admin does not approve within {{signupDays}} days is deleted.
A player's seat stored in the browser is removed when they leave the game. Otherwise it expires after {{seatDays}} days and is removed the next time Quizmoo is opened on that device.
Host accounts, with their quizzes and pictures, stay until the host or the admin deletes them.
The hosting provider's backups may retain deleted data for up to 30 days, after which it is overwritten.

sections.heading: Who else gets your data
paragraphs: Nobody receives it for their own purposes. The service runs at a hosting provider ({{hosting}}), which stores and processes the data only to run the service, as a processor under its data processing terms. If the provider or its parent company is outside the EU/EEA, transfers rely on the safeguards the GDPR requires: an adequacy decision such as the EU–US Data Privacy Framework, or standard contractual clauses.

When an administrator has entered an address for sign-up notices, those e-mails are sent through an e-mail provider ({{mail}}), also acting as a processor. It receives the administrator's address and the notice, which states only how many sign-ups are awaiting approval.

There are no analytics, advertising or social media tools, and the app loads nothing from other sites. The Feedback link for hosts leads to GitHub, a separate service with its own privacy policy; using it is optional.

sections.heading: Your rights
items: Access: you can request a copy of the data stored about you. Hosts: My settings → Account → Download my data.
Rectification of inaccurate data.

Erasure. Hosts: delete your account on My settings → Account; games and quizzes can be deleted at any time. Players: ask the host or write to the contact above with the date of the game, its PIN and your nickname.
Restriction of processing, and objection to processing based on legitimate interest.
Portability: the download above is a machine-readable JSON file.
paragraphs: We answer within one month. As players have no account, we may ask for the game's date, PIN and your nickname to find your data, and never for more than that.

sections.heading: Complaints
paragraphs: You can lodge a complaint with the Hungarian supervisory authority: Nemzeti Adatvédelmi és Információszabadság Hatóság (NAIH), 1055 Budapest, Falk Miksa utca 9–11., ugyfelszolgalat@naih.hu, naih.hu. You can also turn to the supervisory authority where you live or work, or go to court. It helps if you write to the contact above first, so we can resolve the issue.

sections.heading: Children
paragraphs: Hosts must be at least {{age}} years old. Players need no account and give only a nickname; when children play, the host running the event makes sure their parents, school or organisers agree.

sections.heading: Automated decisions and changes
paragraphs: Quizmoo makes no automated decisions about you other than scoring the quiz you play.
When this notice changes, the date above changes too. If a change affects what hosts have accepted, they are asked to accept the new terms at their next login.

cookies.title: Cookies and storage
cookies.intro: Quizmoo uses one cookie, for hosts who log in, and a few entries in your browser's storage, each needed for something you asked for. That is why it does not ask for consent: the ePrivacy Directive and Section 155(4) of the Hungarian Electronic Communications Act allow strictly necessary storage without consent. There are no tracking, analytics or advertising cookies, and nothing is loaded from other sites.

items.session: Keeps you logged in. Page scripts can't read it, and it is sent only to this site over HTTPS. Up to 30 days, or until you log out. On a local network without HTTPS it is called quizmoo_session.
items.player: Your seat in a game (a random code, your nickname and avatar), so a reload brings you back. Removed when you leave the game; otherwise it expires after 2 days and is removed the next time you open Quizmoo.

joining.heading: Joining a game
paragraphs: You need no account and no app: open Quizmoo in your phone's browser.
joining.figure: The join page on a phone

pin.text: Type the 6-digit PIN shown on the projector, or scan the QR code with your phone's camera.

name.text: Type a name, or press Surprise me, and pick an avatar. Use a nickname, not your full name.

team.text: In a team game, join a team or start one. If the host allows it, you can also play on your own.

wait.text: Wait there until the host starts the game, and keep the page open.

answering.heading: Answering
paragraphs: Each question appears on your phone with a timer. Answer before the time runs out.
If the host allows it, you can change your answer while the question runs; the last one counts.
answering.figure: A question on a phone: every answer has its own colour and shape, and the bar shows the time left

multiple.text: Pick every right option, then send. With partial credit each right pick scores and each wrong one cancels a right one; otherwise only the full set counts.

text.text: Type a short answer. Capitals and accents do not matter, and small typos may be accepted if the host allows it.

number.text: Type a number. Some questions accept answers close to it.

order.text: Drag the items into the right order. Only the exact order counts.

poll.text: Give your opinion. There is no right answer and no points.

points.heading: Points
points.figure: A right answer to a 1000-point question, given halfway through the time, the third right answer in a row

right.text: Earns the question's points. A partly right answer to a partial-credit question earns its share; a wrong or missing answer earns nothing.

speed.text: A faster right answer earns more. A right answer in the last moment still earns half.

streak.text: Right answers in a row earn extra: +100 from the second, up to +500.

teams.heading: Playing in a team
paragraphs: Your team plays as one. How its answer is formed depends on the game:
teams.figure: Teammates suggest answers, and the team gives one

captain.text: Everyone suggests an answer, and the captain confirms the one that counts.

majority.text: The answer most members gave counts for the team.

average.text: Each member answers, and the team gets the average of their points.

connection.heading: If you lose the connection
connection.figure: The bar shown while reconnecting, and the menu at the top right

back.text: Your phone remembers you. Reload the page or open the game's link again, in the same browser on the same phone, and you are back with your points.

leave.text: To leave on purpose, choose it in the menu at the top right.

devices.text: You with a laptop or a phone, the players with their phones, and ideally a projector or a TV everyone can see.

items.question: Do players need an account or an app?
items.answer: No. A browser and the PIN are enough. Any phone, tablet or laptop with an up-to-date browser works.

items.question: How many players can join?
items.answer: Up to 60 in one game.

items.question: Someone already has my name. What now?
items.answer: Names are unique within a game. Add a letter or a number, or press Surprise me.

items.question: Why was my name refused?
items.answer: Names are checked against a short list of offensive words. Pick another one.

items.question: A player's phone fell asleep. Are their points lost?
items.answer: No. When they open the game again on the same phone, they are back with their points.

items.question: Can someone join after the start?
items.answer: Only if Players can join late is on and joining is not locked. They get no points for earlier questions.

items.question: Do capitals and accents matter in a typed answer?
items.answer: No: "Győr", "gyor" and "GYŐR" count as the same answer. Whether small typos are accepted is up to the host.

items.question: Why did my answer earn no points?
items.answer: A multiple choice or a put-in-order answer counts only when it is fully right, a poll never earns points, and an answer sent after the time ran out is not taken.

items.question: Two players have the same score. Who is ahead?
items.answer: Neither: they share the place.

items.question: Can I try a quiz before the event?
items.answer: Yes. The phone preview in the editor plays the whole quiz, or start a game and join it from your own phone.

items.question: Do I need a projector?
items.answer: No, but it helps: the whole room follows the questions, the answers and the standings together. Without one, the phones show each question too.

items.question: Does the projector's computer need to log in?
items.answer: No. The projector view needs no login: open it with Open projector, or open the same address on another computer.

items.question: What happens if I close my browser during a game?
items.answer: The game keeps running. Open it again from the home page or from Games, and carry on. A running question still ends on time.

items.question: Someone joined with an unsuitable name. What can I do?
items.answer: Remove them in the lobby with the button on their tile.

items.question: Can I play the quiz again with the same players?
items.answer: Yes. At the end of a game, Play again starts a new game with the same quiz, and the players join it with one tap, keeping their name and avatar.

items.question: Can I bring in questions from a spreadsheet?
items.answer: Yes, with Import on the Quizzes page. Download the template there and fill it in.

items.question: How many questions can a quiz have?
items.answer: Up to 200. Rounds keep a long quiz in order.

items.question: Can I set a game up in advance?
items.answer: Yes. Choose Later in the new game dialog. You can share the game in advance, and it is listed under Games until it starts.

items.question: What does Quizmoo keep about players?
items.answer: Only the nickname they type, their avatar, their team and their answers. No e-mail address, phone number or IP address.

items.question: How long are results kept?
items.answer: For a limited time, then they are deleted automatically; the privacy notice says how long. You can delete a game's results earlier yourself.

items.question: What does Quizmoo store on my device?
items.answer: Only what the app needs, such as the language, the look and your place in a game. The Cookies and storage page lists every item.

items.question: Can I download or delete my data as a host?
items.answer: Yes. In My settings, Account, you can download your data, or delete your account with everything in it.

guide: QUIZMOO QUESTIONS: one question per row, below the header row. Save as CSV (UTF-8), then import it in Quizmoo under Quizzes > Import.
Rows starting with # are notes and are not imported; you may delete them. Keep the columns in this order and leave cells you don't need empty.

type: single (one right answer), multiple (several right answers), true-false, text (players type the answer), number (players type a number), poll (no right answer) or order (players put the answers in order).
question: the question itself, at most 500 characters.
answer 1 to answer 6: what players choose from, 2 to 6 answers of at most 200 characters (single, multiple, poll and order only). For order, write them in the right order; players see them shuffled.
correct, for single: the number of the right answer's column, e.g. 2
correct, for multiple: the numbers of all right answers, e.g. 1, 3
correct, for true-false: true or false
correct, for text: the accepted answers separated by |, e.g. Jupiter | planet Jupiter. Capitals and accents don't matter. Empty: you mark the answers right or wrong during the game.
correct, for number: the right number, e.g. 1848 or 3.5. For poll and order leave it empty.
time: seconds to answer, 5 to 180 (empty: 20). points: 0 to 5000 (empty: 1000). tolerance, for number only: answers this close also count, e.g. 10 (empty: exact).
colour: the question's or round's colour in the editor: red, orange, yellow, green, teal, blue, purple or pink (empty: no colour).
scoring, for multiple only: partial (each right answer picked earns its share, each wrong one cancels a right one) or all (points only for exactly the right answers). Empty: all.

group: starts a round. Write its title in the question column (at most 120 characters), its info in answer 1, and in time and points what its new questions get in the editor. The questions below it belong to the round up to the next group row or a group-end row.
Pictures, game settings and a round's own rules can't go in this file: add them in the editor after importing.
